title: The Live Drop
premise: Casper Dunmore, a private security contractor who has spent six years erasing her past, receives a calendar invitation from Marcus Vane, the handler who died eight months ago, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at 9 p.m. The invitation is a 'live drop'—a dead-man's-switch message containing coordinates to a cache Vane left behind, which holds proof that Casper's former employer, the Halcyon Group, manufactured the identities of its own operatives to embed them as deniable assets inside client organizations, including hers. Hunted by Halcyon's internal cleaner, a man who may be wearing Casper's own erased identity, she must decide whether to trade the cache—her only leverage and the last true record of who she was—to a journalist in exchange for protection, or destroy it and stay invisible forever. In the end, Casper broadcasts the archive publicly, sacrificing her anonymity but reclaiming authorship of her own name, while the cleaner, revealed to be another fabricated self, chooses to vanish rather than kill the one person who understands him.
about_author: Marguerite Galloway is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms she is still contractually barred from naming. She lives off-grid on the Welsh coast, where she writes thrillers about people whose paperwork matters more than their pulse.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Working a routine protection detail in Rotterdam, Casper receives a calendar invite from Marcus Vane—dead eight months—for tomorrow at 9 p.m. She checks the metadata: sent from his verified account, timestamped after his death. The chapter establishes her paranoia, her go-bag ritual, and ends with her deciding, against every instinct, to open the attachment.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Flashback interwoven with present preparation: how Vane recruited her six years ago, how he taught her to build an identity like a load-bearing wall. She burns her current cover, empties accounts, and drives toward the meeting point—a decommissioned ferry terminal—cataloguing what she knows about her own death protocols.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock, Empty Pier
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. No one comes. Instead, a dead drop: a burner phone taped beneath a bollard, preloaded with a single video—Vane, recorded before his death, telling her Halcyon built her identity from scratch and that the proof sits in a cache only she can unlock. A car's headlights sweep the pier. She runs.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to Her Name
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Wren (the cleaner). Introduced coldly efficient, Wren reports to Halcyon director Ingrid Sølv that the Vane cache has surfaced. His file photo unsettles even him: it's Casper's face, pre-transition, under a name she supposedly abandoned. He requests the termination contract himself.

chapters.title: Cache Mechanics
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Holed up in a safehouse outside Ghent, Casper deciphers Vane's riddle: the cache requires two keys—her biometric signature and a passphrase buried in a memory she has deliberately suppressed. The chapter dramatizes her resistance to remembering, ending with the first fragment surfacing: a hospital corridor, a clipboard, her old name spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Sølv's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Ingrid Sølv. Halcyon's director reviews the 'Fabrication Program': forty-one operatives given synthetic identities and seeded into client organizations as leverage. Vane was the program's architect turned whistleblower. Sølv orders the cache destroyed and the program's other ghosts quietly retired. Power shown as bureaucratic tidiness.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Contacted by Dana Okonkwo, an investigative journalist who received a fragment of Vane's archive, Casper meets her in a Brussels library. Dana offers publication and legal shield in exchange for exclusive access to the cache. Casper refuses—the archive contains her real name. First negotiation, first refusal.

chapters.title: Passphrase, Part One
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Following the memory trail to a clinic in Antwerp where her identity was manufactured, Casper finds the intake room preserved exactly as Vane promised. Sensory triggers crack the suppression wider: she recalls consenting to the program—or believing she did. The distinction between choice and coercion begins to blur.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper/Wren. Wren closes in through hotel CCTV and a compromised contact. Casper spots the surveillance pattern too late and improvises an escape through the Antwerp rail station, using a tradecraft trick Vane taught her—one Wren recognizes, because he was trained by the same man.

chapters.title: Brothers in Fabrication
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Alone in a safe flat, Wren examines his own file and confronts the possibility that his memories—mother, childhood, a drowning brother—are inserts. He tests one against public records and finds nothing. He doesn't report this to Sølv. First fracture in loyalty.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The passphrase resolves into a date and a sentence Vane made her repeat during training, which she now understands was never training—it was key-making. But unlocking requires her to be physically present at the cache site: a Halcyon black-site facility in the Ardennes, decommissioned on paper, very much alive in practice.

chapters.title: Dana's Deadline
chapters.summary: POV: Dana Okonkwo. Her editor kills the story under legal pressure; sources go silent; she realizes Halcyon has infiltrated her newsroom. She reaches Casper anyway, offering what she has left: the fragment archive and a warning that Halcyon knows the cache location. Trust forms between two women with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Paper Building
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Using credentials from her contractor days, Casper enters the Ardennes facility posing as an external auditor. Inside she finds the Fabrication Program's living archive: rooms of files for identities, including dozens still active—people walking around wearing invented lives. She photographs everything.

chapters.title: Interrogation Room 4
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In the facility's memory-vault, Casper recovers her original intake recording: she didn't volunteer. Vane falsified her consent to save her from someone—flashback reveals she witnessed a Halcyon-ordered killing years ago. The passphrase completes itself. Then alarms trigger; Wren has arrived.

chapters.title: Two Keys, One Door
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper/Wren. Cat-and-mouse through the facility's corridors. They finally meet face to face at the cache vault—and Wren hesitates, because her file explains his life better than his own memories do. He lets her open the vault, then reports the cache 'compromised and empty.'

chapters.title: What the Cache Holds
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The drive contains the full program ledger: all forty-one operatives, the consent forgeries, the client leverage operations, and Vane's confession—including his role in building Casper's false past. Betrayal and vindication arrive together. She must choose: trade it to Dana, or burn it and disappear for good.

chapters.title: Sølv Closes the Net
chapters.summary: POV: Ingrid Sølv. Discovering Wren's deception, Søvl activates contingency protocol: she releases Casper's real identity to international databases, making her visible, trackable, desperate—invisibility revoked as punishment. Simultaneously she offers Wren a promotion contingent on delivering Casper's body.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. For the first time in six years, Casper cannot move without cameras finding her. Safehouses burn; contacts cut her off. Cornered in a Rotterdam tenement, she makes the decision the whole book has bent toward: if she can't be invisible, she'll be unmistakable. She calls Dana.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Casper/Dana. From a moving van with satellite uplink, they publish the entire archive—every operative, every forgery, Sølv's own fabricated history included—as Halcyon's strike team converges. Wren arrives not to stop them but to hold the door, buying the upload time with gunfire and his resignation letter.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV: multiple brief vignettes. The broadcast detonates globally: clients sever contracts, governments open inquiries, operatives learn their names are inventions. Sølv is detained at a private airfield; some fabricated operatives grieve, some are relieved. Casper watches from a ferry deck, anonymous again—but by choice, not design.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Weeks later, in a small coastal town, Casper reads her own file in a published leak like a stranger's biography. She visits Vane's unmarked grave and leaves the burner phone on the stone. She applies for a passport under her original name—not the fabricated one, the real one she'd fled. Identity reclaimed, not restored.

chapters.title: Live Drop
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Somewhere far north, the cleaner who let her live receives a calendar invitation from an account that shouldn't exist: Casper Dunmore, tomorrow, 9 p.m. He packs a bag, almost smiles, and goes. The cycle of handlers, drops, and chosen meetings continues—but this time, attendance is voluntary.
